## Engine-fix implementation plan (agreed 2026-08-26; next session starts here)

### Binding problem statement (user, 2026-08-26)

Solve 12-75 tick sequences to the GLOBAL optimum with GIVEN key inputs. The only job is finding the yaw values for those keys; in-game that means the sine buckets (byte-exact). The current algorithm solves well, but only in continuous space; the overarching problem is that we cannot find the in-game feasible solution, and solving must also be fast. Two capabilities: FAST = find any in-game feasible solve as fast as possible; OPTIMIZE = given a time budget, search and optimize a direction objective (MAX X, MIN Z, ...), attempting the in-game GLOBAL optimum. Longer runs are handled by receding-horizon multi-segment solving, and that is where the issues arise; a path diverges for two reasons: (1) sine quantization, ~e-5..e-6 per tick, and (2) inertia, whose error stacks heavily and can reach full-block divergence; the current mitigation is branching on inertia ticks. This inner use case gets ALL current effort. The second use case, stratfinding (searching the inputs themselves, no-turn discovery), is split to #424 as a parked follow-up and is deliberately not being planned further now.

Scope notes: instances longer than ~75 ticks (e.g. j003, n=176) are exercised through the receding-horizon window path, so the per-window solves stay inside the 12-75t envelope; the interior-modulus/chatter behavior also occurs WITHIN windows (thousand ticks 0-15, j153 first half), so the chatter-rounding item remains in scope. Cross-window divergence is exactly the H4 finding: interface velocity errors amplify 6.5-10.1x downstream, which is why windows must chain the exact byte-exact exit state and certify per window instead of translating continuous solutions per segment.

Follow-up to the Step 1 verdicts above. The question this plan answers: the current engine cannot find good in-game solutions (multi-jump jitter and missed solutions, knife-edge no-solves, the j003 regression). This plan is INNER-solver only: fixed inputs, find per-tick facings. No input search anywhere in it; the grammar / easy-class / pool-driver material lives in #424 and is not part of this build.

### Root cause to fix, mapped (all measured, see ARCH2-STEP1-SIMPLIFY.md)

| Engine symptom | Measured root cause | Fix | Provenance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Multi-jump jitter, missed findable solutions, re-solve fragility (thousand-class; roc give-up) | CostateDualSolver full-modulus recovery has a structural feasibility floor (pgres is a recovery meter; at the kink some costate g_t = 0, no multiplier yields a feasible recovery; floor frozen over 300k iterations while the dual value is tight to 1e-3) | Fold-and-replay incumbent driver: solve disk SOCP, replay via ExactJumpModel, extract gate pattern from replay velocities, re-solve on the folded model, iterate to the fixed point. Dual demoted to bound + deep-node dive + tail pinning. Never gate on pgres. | Mechanism measured in the PoC: fidelity 1.3e-2 to 1.5e-4 in 2 rounds, every run |
| Knife-edge captures return nothing | Corridors 1e-4..9e-5 wide; no incumbent mechanism can land in them; nearest-bucket snapping additionally loses up to ~5e-4 per tick on legacy chains (sine pair-norm noise 4.8e-5, true argmax up to +-50 buckets off) | Wall-homotopy ladder (relax compiled wall RHS 0.05 -> 0.01 -> 0.002 -> 0, warm-start each rung) + per-wall signed SLP margins measured at the replayed anchor, re-anchored each round + bucket-window leaf scan + pinned-bucket walk + free-start ulp nudge | Homotopy measured as the only cold knife-edge discovery mechanism (j154 session best, zero human data); margins + pinning converged in 3 rounds every time |
| j003 (n=176): FAST worse point, THOROUGH hangs | Continuous optimum is modulus-interior on ALL 176 ticks: with fixed keys the byte realization is facing chatter; costate silent everywhere, all gates root-ambiguous, so the current recovery stack has nothing to offer | NEW build: chatter rounding. Track the disk solution's velocity trajectory through the friction chain and choose per-tick grid facings from a bucket window to realize interior thrust (sum-up-rounding style tracking or a small per-axis deviation DP), then fold + replay + margin-polish. Plus 3-way gate branching concentrated on the low-velocity tail | New; neither the engine nor the PoC has this today |
| Local search gets basin-stuck (ILS/SLP polish one family; bucket windows are basin-local) | The fixed-pattern iteration is local by construction; nothing moves basins with bounds | NEW build: the certified arc + gate B&B (ARCH-2 core). Arc bisection with chord + endpoint tangent cuts, branch order from the disk solve's own throttled-tick list, 3-way gates only on replay-falsified folds + the tail, incumbents from the driver above, terminate at gap=0 | New; this exists precisely because the local loop cannot certify or escape basins |
| j003 THOROUGH deadline overrun | Solve exceeds its own deadline with no anytime result | Anytime discipline: every fold round and homotopy rung yields a replayable incumbent; deadlines respected at round granularity | Engineering hygiene, ties to the Fast/Optimize tier contract |

### Why this is not "porting the weak Python solver"

The PoC's measured discovery failures are all OUTER failures, i.e. failures of searching key schedules: 0 incumbents cold on the exact-circle MIQCP (500k+ nodes), cold search death on j154 before homotopy existed, and 0-for-3 on cold rediscovery of the easy j1150 structure (the unbuilt pool driver). Within a fixed schedule, the PoC solves were the healthy part (pattern solves OPTIMAL in 14-18 s, translation loops converging in 2-3 rounds). The engine's problem IS the fixed-schedule problem. So the port takes only the mechanisms that measured well for exactly that setting, and the two genuinely new pieces (chatter rounding, certified B&B) are the answer to what the Python loop structurally could not do: realize interior thrust, move basins, and certify.

### Falsification pre-check (do this before writing Java)

Run the fold + margins + pinning loop through the existing python harness (research/copt) on 2-3 FIXED-INPUT engine failures and check it lands byte-exact incumbents where the engine currently returns nothing or jitter: one thousand-class capture (needs the save, see below), one knife-edge hpk capture with its schedule fixed, optionally a j003 chatter prototype in python. If this fails, stop and rethink before any port.

### Staged build plan with acceptance gates

Two shippable milestones: M1 = the discovery stack (fixes FAST and OPTIMIZE quality), M2 = certified B&B + the mandatory cleanup (completes this ticket). Sizes: S = hours, M = 1-3 days, L = 1-2 weeks. Every stage gates on numbers; nothing proceeds on a red gate.

0. **M0 falsification pre-check** (S; python/COPT only, NO Java until this passes): run the fold + margins + pinning loop through research/copt on struct-thousand-1dup2 with the schedule fixed from the rows, judged byte-exact via NoTurnReplay (target: lands >= 6523.30 where the engine jitters); the same loop on one knife-edge hpk capture with fixed schedule; a python chatter-rounding prototype on j003 windows (target: the -31.29 class byte-exact). GATE: all three land byte-exact; any failure stops the port and revises the design.
1. **Component inventory** (S; the ticket's agreed step 2): keep/replace/delete table against the reduced design, covering DiskSocpKernel, pattern-aware JumpLinearModel + velocityWalls, JumpConstraintCompiler, ExactJumpModel, SlpSolve/TrustRegionLp, LongRunSolver, RunTicksSearch, CostateDualSolver call sites, and every recovery graph node (BoundPrunedRecovery, SphereDecodeSnap, GateMip, MiniCmaSolve, SeamSweepRecovery, RelaxationRecovery, LevelSetAscent). Posted here as a comment.
2. **M1a fold + fixed-point driver in core** (M): clamp-free disk solve -> replay -> extract gate pattern from replay velocities -> folded re-solve, iterate to the fixed point (<= 4 rounds); every round emits a replayable incumbent (anytime by construction); FreeP0 supported; keep-alive violations detected at replay flip that tick's pattern entry with bounded retries. GATE: thousand solves >= 6523.30, bit-identical across 5 re-solves; zero corpus feasibility regressions at FAST.
3. **M1b wall-homotopy ladder** (M): staged wall-RHS relaxation (0.05 / 0.01 / 0.002 / 0) on the compiled walls, warm-started rungs, driver-integrated; >= 2e-6 collision clearance baked into the solve (pad/floor edges exempt). GATE: at least 2 knife-edge hpk captures that currently return nothing produce byte-exact feasible solves.
4. **M1c anchor-local margins** (S-M): per-wall signed byte-minus-linear offsets at the replayed anchor, re-anchored per round, never persisted across pattern or schedule changes. GATE: knife-edge expects converge to maxViolation 0 in <= 3 rounds.
5. **M1d bucket-window leaf** (S-M): replace nearest-bucket snapping with a window scan (legacy +-50, 26.x +-3) capped to active-wall neighborhoods, plus the pinned-bucket walk and free-start ulp nudge; must not break the sphere-snap yaw-lock save/playback path. GATE: no corpus objective give-back; knife-edge targets hit.
6. **M1e chatter rounding** (M; the j003 fix): triggered by the disk solve's throttled-tick fraction; per-axis tracking DP over bucket windows realizes interior thrust; fold + margin polish after; explicit tail gate handling. GATE: j003 >= OLD's -31.2999 at FAST and THOROUGH, inside deadline, expect green.
7. **M1f engine wiring + budget discipline** (M): the driver becomes the primary recovery in the solver graph; CostateDualSolver demoted to bound provider; ClosestMiss / no-solution panel fed from driver rounds; SolverTrace events; deadlines respected at round granularity; development behind a temporary system property that is REMOVED before ship. M1 SHIP GATE: full CorpusBench vs the STEP-9 baselines with 0 feasibility regressions and the win set holding; j003 + thousand + knife-edge expects green; FAST floor recovered (median cold <= ~80 ms, p90 <= 562 ms); slow suite + determinism guard green; zero flags.
8. **M1 QA + ship** (S + user): author the new expects (thousand-1-dup2 at 6523.30772; fixed-schedule j1150 at -2805.2990460856336 and j154 at -1599.7237570, all tagged SlowSolverTests); update TESTS.md; in-game byte-exact QA through SimulatorEntity on 1.8.9 + Fabric (thousand, j003, one knife-edge, the sphere-snap yaw-lock captures); feature branch off dev; the user handles all git.
9. **M2a certified arc + gate B&B** (L): nodes = arc brackets + gate fixings; relaxation = DiskSocpKernel + chord + endpoint tangent cuts; branch order from throttled/degenerate ticks; 3-way gates only on replay-falsified folds + the tail; incumbents from the M1 driver + costate dive at depth + tail pinning; dual value as prune bound; gap=0 termination with the running gap mapped onto FAST/OPTIMIZE. GATE: certified equal-or-better on the expect corpus; first certified byte-exact global on small captures; root bounds validated against the COPT oracle.
10. **M2b mandatory cleanup** (M; the ticket's agreed step 3): delete subsumed recovery components per the inventory, one recovery owner, net LOC reduction, remaining FAST-floor recovery, zero flags. GATE: STEP-9 rubric PASS-on-structure; full suite + corpus green.
11. **M2 QA + ship, close this ticket** (S + user).

Judgment calls a reviewer should scrutinize (declared, not measured): the chatter-rounding design in M1e (the only unmeasured mechanism, which is why M0 prototypes it first), the keep-alive pattern-flip retry in M1a, the M1a-M1f ordering, the ~80 ms floor target and round caps, and two-loader QA where the rules require one.

Explicitly dropped or demoted per Step 1: FBBT as gate-fixer (node arc tightening only), the costate as incumbent engine, the k-gon dual simplex (build on measured need only), pseudocosts, any frozen a-priori translation layer, any velocity-window interface.

### Regression cases (status: mostly in place)

Existing, run as the gate for every step:
- ProblemsTest: folder-driven with 46 expect files under problems/solve (j003.expect.json included), plus problems/closedform. Full solver suite = `./gradlew :core:test -PslowTests` (CI always runs it).
- CorpusBench: 126 solvable captures, FAST + THOROUGH tiers, committed OLD/NEW baseline TSVs from STEP 9 under docs/research/solver-rework-2026-08/benchmark/ with compare.py. Re-run: `PKC_CORPUS=1 PKC_CORPUS_TIER=FAST ./gradlew :core:cleanTest :core:test --tests '*CorpusBench'`.
- Named acceptance targets: j003 must reach the OLD objective (-31.2999, continuous bound -31.3) at BOTH tiers with no deadline overrun; j021-rinav1-01 optimize target 1067.8638 (the graph-path gate); zero feasibility regressions corpus-wide (STEP-9 standard); the STEP-9 FAST win set must not give back.
- Determinism guard (OI-17) and the in-game byte-exact QA rule for touched loaders.

To author next session (small tasks):
- Knife-edge inner-problem expects: fix the schedules from the byte-exact no-turn results and let the engine solve facings only, expecting equal-or-better byte-exact objectives. Targets: j1150 pure no-turn X@49 = -2805.2990460856336 (artifacts research/copt/data/noturn-j1150-p2-decode/replay.json) and j154 corrected-spec X@39 = -1599.7237570 (D2 artifacts). These become ProblemsTest cases tagged SlowSolverTests.
- thousand/1-dup2: IN REPO since 2026-08-26 as core/src/test/resources/captures/thousand-1-dup2.json (struct export research/copt/data/struct-thousand-1dup2.json; the recorded strat replays byte-exact clean at 6523.307720901059, viol 0.0). Still needs an expect.json (target 6523.30772). Probes on the original instance now confirm the H3 diagnosis: the dual recovery floor is structural (violation plateaued at ~3.6-3.8 blocks over 60k..300k iterations while the dual value still creeps; near-zero costate tick 3.1e-3 vs median 0.81 at the best multiplier), the disk optimum is modulus-interior on ticks 0-15 (overlapping chatter zone t13-17; the t26-30 chatter is the costate-cancellation kind). Inertia decomposition of that floor, measured after review: the probe, like CostateDualSolver itself, is clamp-free; on this capture ignoring inertia shifts the warm trajectory by 4.5e-2 on the objective and makes the byte-exact-feasible warm point look 5.6e-2 infeasible in the clamp-free model, so missing inertia explains the ~5e-2 scale, while the ~3.6-block floor is dominated by full-modulus recovery forced onto the 16 interior-modulus ticks (slack up to 0.206/tick, friction-amplified ~10x). Folding fixes the former, interior-capable incumbents the latter; both are in the build order. The falsification pre-check can run on this capture immediately.
- A j003 chatter-prototype target: the disk bound -31.3 is the ceiling; the expect stays the OLD -31.2999 until the prototype shows better.

Provenance for all numbers: `docs/research/global-solver-2026-08/ARCH2-STEP1-SIMPLIFY.md`.
